note: Hebrew me'ever leYarden means "beyond the Jordan"; the KJV renders from the camp's viewpoint east of the river, but the phrase is a fixed term for the Transjordan opposite Jericho.
Hebrew me'odekha means "from your existence on", i.e. as long as you have lived; the KJV's supplied words make it the length of ownership.
Hebrew 'ir Mo'av here is probably the place name Ir/Ar of Moab (cf. 21:15, 28), not an unnamed city.

kjv: into the high places of Baal, that thence he (Balaam) might see
mine: to Bamoth-baal, and from there he (Balaam) saw
note: Hebrew bamot ba'al is likely the place name Bamoth-baal (cf. 21:19-20), and wayyar' is a plain narrative "and he saw", not a purpose clause.
